result.title: Can JEV Support Clinical Trial Criteria Assessment?
result.summary: Clinical trial prescreening requires distinguishing unmet conditions from insufficient evidence in patient records. Given patient records, criterion questions, and predefined answer options, we retrospectively compared JEV, a non-generative decision model returning native option probabilities, with schema-constrained Qwen Flash across 2,048 test patient-condition pairs from TrialGPT and question-answer datasets derived from MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, all evaluated under strict Zero Data Retention (ZDR) policies to ensure clinical data privacy. Both models assessed conditions individually or in batches sharing the same patient context, with performance measured against reference labels. In batch mode, JEV and Qwen achieved similar macro-F1 scores on TrialGPT (0.652 vs. 0.660) and MIMIC-IV (0.807 vs. 0.814), whereas JEV substantially outperformed Qwen on MIMIC-III (0.768 vs. 0.534; $Δ$ = +0.234, 95% CI: 0.187-0.281). This advantage largely reflected higher recall for conditions labeled as having insufficient information (56.3% vs. 9.9%). Across all three datasets, JEV also had lower observed median job latency (1.18-1.40 vs. 2.80-8.90 s) and 53%-74% lower estimated cost per condition. These findings position JEV as an initial assessment component that provides criterion-level judgments and flags potential information gaps for review. JEV's observed errors in interpreting clinical evidence underscore the need to verify its outputs against patient records before they inform eligibility decisions.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在临床试验入组标准的预筛任务上，比较了非生成式决策模型 JEV（直接输出候选项概率）与结构约束的 Qwen Flash，用 TrialGPT 及 MIMIC-III/IV 衍生的问答数据评测宏 F1、时延与成本，并强调「信息不足」类条件的召回差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其区分「条件不满足」与「证据不足」并据此标记信息缺口的设定，可能与 LVR 中的停止决策、弃权与证据筛选评价相通；非生成式概率读出与逐条件计时/成本核算也提供了可供核查的对照口径，但与视觉推理无直接关联。
